Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: BoN is the regulator and oversees the NPS: Payment System Management Act 14 of 2023 assigns BoN powers to regulate/oversee NPS and approve payment system rules, membership criteria, and issue directives.[Payment System Management Act 14 of 2023 (LAC)](https://www.lac.org.na/laws/annoSTAT/Payment%20System%20Management%20Act%2014%20of%202023.pdf) For IPS, BoN is directly implementing via its subsidiary IPN, and NPCI is deploying the solution within BoN environment (test/build phase).[BoN RFP for IPN reconciliation & attestation tool](https://www.bon.com.na/CMSTemplates/Bon/Files/bon.com.na/e4/e4467afa-167e-4773-aa09-b1c286d25223.pdf)

Definition: Whether national data protection or privacy legislation exists and explicitly covers payment transaction data, including provisions on data collection, storage, sharing, retention, and user rights over their payment data.
Comments: No enacted comprehensive data protection law could be confirmed; available sources describe an un-enacted Data Protection Bill and indicate Namibia lacks enacted data protection legislation.[ITLawCo – Namibia Data Protection Bill](https://itlawco.com/focus-areas/data-protection-and-privacy/namibias-data-protection-bill-moving-towards-privacy-and-data-security/)

Definition: Whether payment system governance explicitly includes mechanisms to ensure inclusivity and represent interests of vulnerable populations, including provisions for input from all participant types, consumer representatives, small providers, or explicit financial inclusion mandates in governance documents.
Comments: No explicit pro-poor governance requirements (e.g., mandated consumer/low-income representation) were found in BoN PSD-6 determination on payment system operator authorization/governance; it focuses on governance/fitness & probity, risk, and reporting.[BoN PSD-6 (Gov Gazette No. 8382)](https://www.lac.org.na/laws/2024/8382.pdf)

Definition: Whether the scheme rules governing payment system participation, pricing structure, technical requirements, security standards, and conduct are publicly accessible via website, public repository, or on request. Transparency indicator.
Comments: Payment system operators must draft rules covering governance, access criteria, risk management, finality, standards, fees, and rights/obligations for BoN approval, but PSD-6 does not require public disclosure; forms are marked confidential.[BoN PSD-6 (Gov Gazette No. 8382)](https://www.lac.org.na/laws/2024/8382.pdf)

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: Namibia has an upgraded national EFT system (NamPay) including a near-real-time credit transfer stream (NRTC), implemented under BoN Payment System Directive PSD7 as described by Nedbank.[Nedbank Namibia – NamPay](https://nedbank.com.na/content/nedbank-namibia/desktop/na/en/aboutus/legal/Nam-Pay.html) Namibia is also implementing a new national “Instant Payment Solution (IPS)” / “Instant Payment Programme (IPP)” operated via BoN subsidiary Instant Payments Namibia (IPN), with integration testing completed and UAT underway; launch expected in Q3 2026 (per 2026/27 budget speech coverage).[New Era](https://neweralive.na/namibia-draws-closer-to-instant-government-payments/)
